RE: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
Reference Number: POC-9DD444765E-23652
Member: Cameron Grant, Member ID W314904804
Denied Service: Rotator cuff repair, CPT 29827
Date of Notice: 2026-08-08
Appeal Deadline: 2027-02-04

Dear Appeals Reviewer,

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for CPT 29827 (arthroscopic rotator cuff repair), dated 2026-08-08, reference number POC-9DD444765E-23652. The notice states the denial reason as: "the requested procedure does not meet the plan's applicable medical policy and clinical review criteria for medical necessity." I am requesting that Molina reverse this determination and approve the surgery.

**1. The specific criteria applied to this denial have not been disclosed to me, and I am requesting them.**

The notice I received does not identify the title, policy number, or specific criteria used to reach this decision. I have researched Molina's public medical policy library and located Molina Clinical Policy No. 404, "Shoulder Arthroscopy Guidelines." That document states:

"This policy addresses arthroscopic procedures when performed as an elective, non-emergent technique for disease pathology that will cause progressive destruction. For Rotator Cuff Repair, please refer to MCG Shoulder Arthroscopy Guidelines."

An earlier version of the same Molina document states: "Please see MCG criteria for rotator cuff repair."

I have not been able to obtain or review the actual text of the MCG guideline that Molina's own policy identifies as governing rotator cuff repair — that document is proprietary and was not provided with my denial notice, and I am **not** quoting or attributing any specific language from it because I have not seen it. I am formally requesting, under my right to the specific medical standards/clinical review criteria used to make this decision, that Molina provide me and my surgeon, Dr. Okafor, with a full copy of the exact MCG criteria (title, edition, and section) applied to CPT 29827 in my case, so that we can respond point-by-point to any specific unmet criterion.

**2. The clinical record supports medical necessity under the general standards Molina applies to shoulder arthroscopic surgery.**

While the precise rotator cuff repair criteria have not been disclosed to me, Molina's own published policy for related shoulder arthroscopy procedures (debridement, diagnostic arthroscopy, labral repair) is built around the same categories of clinical evidence: severe pain/functional loss, abnormal exam findings, failed conservative treatment of at least three months, and confirmatory imaging. My record documents all of these elements for a full-thickness rotator cuff tear:

- **Duration and severity of symptoms:** 24 months of progressive shoulder pain, unrelieved by rest, with resulting inability to lift the arm above shoulder height or sleep on the affected side.
- **Failed conservative management, well beyond three months:**
  - Supervised physical therapy focused on rotator cuff strengthening and scapular mechanics — 8 weeks, 2026-05-20 through 2026-07-15, 20 visits completed, documented in the physical therapy discharge note.
  - NSAIDs for 8 months with inadequate relief.
  - Corticosteroid injection on 2026-06-08, yielding only 4 weeks of partial relief.
- **Abnormal physical examination findings:** Positive provocative testing on the affected side, with range of motion limited by pain.
- **Confirmatory imaging:** MRI of the shoulder dated 2026-06-05 showing a full-thickness supraspinatus tear measuring 1.8 cm with grade 2 fatty atrophy.
- **No disqualifying comorbidities:** No active infection, no untreated substance use, BMI 29, non-smoker.

Given the documented full-thickness tear with fatty atrophy, the well-documented and prolonged trial of conservative therapy that has failed, and the significant functional impairment, I believe this record supports medical necessity for surgical repair. I am not asserting that this is a verbatim match to the MCG rotator cuff repair criteria, since that document has not been shared with me — but I am asking Molina to apply its own disclosed criteria to this record and to explain, in writing, exactly which specific criterion is considered unmet if the denial is upheld.

**3. Requested action.**

1. Reverse the denial and authorize CPT 29827 for Cameron Grant, performed by Dr. Okafor.
2. In the alternative, provide the complete, specific MCG (or other) clinical review criteria applied to this determination, including the exact policy title, number, and effective/revision date, so that my provider and I can supplement the record accordingly within the appeal window.
3. Confirm receipt of this appeal in writing and provide the applicable internal appeal decision timeframe.

I am appealing within the stated 180-day window (by 2027-02-04). Please contact my surgeon's office, Dr. Okafor [orthopedic surgery practice name, address, phone, and NPI — not stated in the records provided], for any additional records needed, including the physical therapy discharge note, MRI report dated 2026-06-05, and injection/medication records referenced above.

Thank you for your prompt attention to this appeal.

Sincerely,

Cameron Grant
Member ID: W314904804

Enclosures: [PT discharge note; MRI report 2026-06-05; injection record 2026-06-08; medication history; surgeon's letter of medical necessity — to be attached as available]
